blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — While the Senate impeachment court’s ruling allowed a lower minimum vote requirement to convict Vice President Sara Duterte if some senator-judges are absent, it did not change the conviction threshold itself. Batangas Rep. Gerville Luistro clarified this situation on Thursday in a press briefing at the Batasang Pambansa. Luistro was asked whether the impeachment court’s decision on Wednesday meant that a lower threshold to convict Duterte is now allowed. The lawmaker is the lead public prosecutor for Duterte’s impeachment trial She maintained that the 1987 Constitution’s two-thirds requirement for conviction still stands. “The threshold was not lowered, two-thirds remains […]...
